question.text: Jessica's circular swimming pool has a radius of $10\,\textrm{ft}.$ What is the area of the pool?
question.explanation: The formula for the area of a circle is $\mathcal{A}=\pi r^2,$ so the area of Jessica's pool is \begin{align*} \mathcal{A} &= \pi r^2 \\[3pt] &= \pi \cdot 10^2 \\[3pt] &= 100\pi \,\textrm{ft}^2. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating the Area of a Circle Given the Diameter

question.text: What is the area of a circle that has a diameter of $8\,\text{m}?$
question.explanation:
The radius of a circle is half the diameter. So, the radius of our circle is $r=4.$

Therefore, the area is

\begin{align*} \mathcal{A} &= \pi r^2 \\[3pt] &= \pi \cdot 4^2 \\[3pt] &= 16 \pi\,\text{m}^2. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating the Area of a Circle Given the Diameter

question.text: What is the diameter of a circle if its area is $9\pi\,\text{km}^2?$
question.explanation:
The formula for the area of a circle is $\mathcal{A}=\pi r^2$, where $r$ is the radius. Therefore,

\begin{align*} \require{cancel} \mathcal{A} &= \pi r^2 \\[3pt] 9\pi &= \pi r^2 \\[3pt] 9\cancel{\pi} &= \cancel{\pi} r^2 \\[3pt] r^2 &= 9\\[3pt] r &= 3\,\text{km}. \end{align*}

Therefore, the diameter is

\[ d=2\cdot r= 2\cdot 3=6\,\text{km}. \]
